effort: Maintain rapid stance-support force with no planned jump landings, preparing for a controlled final comparison exposure.
brief: The emphasis is force expression with supported feet and a quiet pelvis, preserving training quality without an impact requirement. E1 anchors quick knee-flexed ankle force. Long-lever hip drive, split-base held-implement drive, resisted hip extension, dorsiflexion and hip abduction cover the distinct support/recovery actions. Every rapid task is brief and light; familiar light foot/adductor control precedes six challenging strength roles.
marker: For each leg, compare the two sets of three heel rises: similar heel height, steady small knee bend, no ankle roll and a visibly crisp rise. Forefoot stays grounded. This is execution consistency, not measured power, tendon stiffness or clearance for more impact.
review: Class 10 prescribed 24 landings including twelve unilateral events and six primary rounds. No actual response is known. Class 11 uses zero planned flight and retains six primary rounds as a deliberate support option; this is not a claim the athlete needs a taper or is sore. Any actual competition schedule still governs placement.
sequence: E1 is the main rapid ankle-force observation. E2/E3 express hip force while supported; E4–E6 accelerate individual leg/foot actions against light resistance without turning them into running drills or a continuous circuit.

E.name: Supported Single-Leg Bent-Knee Calf Rise — fast concentric
E.job: Main no-impact task: express ankle force quickly under a stable flexed-knee single-leg support position.
E.cue: Stable hand support, small knee bend, working forefoot grounded. Rise quickly and lower over 2 s while holding approximately the same knee angle. Bodyweight or a very light DB only if speed/control remain. Use more hand unloading or a small kickstand foot instead if bodyweight is too demanding.

E.name: Long-Lever Heel-Bridge Drive — fast concentric
E.job: Express hip extension with a more open knee angle so hamstrings contribute without a jumping demand.
E.cue: Supine, heels grounded farther from hips than a normal bridge, knees still softly bent. Drive hips up a small amount quickly, return over 2 s; feet/shoulders never launch. Bring heels closer for cramping or back arch. This changes lever/joint position, not a new hip-extension family.

E.name: Split-Stance Held-Ball Hip Drive — no release
E.family: asymmetric rapid force into a retained implement
E.job: Accelerate a light external mass using the legs/hips while the split base controls pelvic rotation.
E.cue: Light ball held low close to body, short split stance; shallow knee/hip bend then drive tall quickly while carrying the ball only to waist/lower-chest height. No release, jump, overhead lift or arm-only heave. Return over 2 s; reduce load/stance offset for twisting.

E.name: Supported Band Hip Extension — fast back drive
E.family: rapid hip extension with pelvis fixed
E.job: Accelerate the thigh backward through a small hip-extension range without substituting lumbar movement.
E.cue: Light band at working ankle to a verified low anchor in front, stable hand support. Stance foot planted; drive the working thigh slightly behind the body with knee soft, return over 2 s. Keep pelvis facing forward. Reduce band/range for back arch or pelvic rotation.

E.name: Seated Band Dorsiflexion — fast toe-up
E.job: Accelerate forefoot lift against light resistance for the foot-clearance component of leg recovery.
E.cue: Sit with heel supported, light band around forefoot to a verified low anchor ahead. Pull toes/forefoot toward shin quickly, return over 2 s; knee/heel stay still. Reduce tension for toe curling or whole-leg pulling. No forced end-range stretch.

E.name: Supported Band Hip Abduction — quick lateral lift
E.job: Express short-range lateral hip force while keeping the stance pelvis controlled.
E.cue: Suitable light loop around ankles, stable hand support. Stance foot planted; move the other straight-but-soft leg a small distance sideways quickly, return over 2 s and reset. No side step, torso lean or pelvis hike. Use less tension/range for compensation.

S.name: Short-Foot Drill — bilateral supported stance
S.job: Maintain familiar light active-arch support while limiting unnecessary novelty before the final exposure.
S.cue: Both feet supported, one target arch gently shortens while toes stay long and heel remains grounded; relax between holds. Use seated execution instead if standing causes toe grip. Do not increase hold force to create fatigue.

S.name: Side-Lying Hip Adduction
S.job: Retain easy adductor force for pelvic support, complementing the rapid abductor task.
S.cue: Top foot supported on floor in front, bottom leg straight; lift bottom thigh 2 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s without rolling. Bodyweight only, smaller range if effort becomes strenuous. Stop for groin discomfort or cramping.

P.name: Split Squat — two dumbbells at sides
P.cue: Floor split stance, front foot planted, pelvis square; lower 2 s and rise firmly for 1 s. Reduce load/range for collapse or balance loss. Use one DB with stable hand support instead of two unsupported DBs if needed; counts stay the same.
P.job: Maintain one challenging stance-leg knee/hip force set per leg.
P.decision: Return to the familiar split-squat pattern at 1 × 6 per leg for consolidation. Same working count as Class 10's one-set step-up; do not infer equivalent load.

P.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
P.cue: Soft knees, hips back, DBs close; lower 3 s and rise in 1 s. Stop the descent before back rounding; reduce load/range if the hinge becomes spinal movement.
P.job: Retain a small loadable hip-hinge force exposure.

P.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated dumbbells
P.cue: Both legs together, knees near 90°, heels start on floor, hands secure DBs on lower thighs above knees. Rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Reduce load for bounce/lost heel height. If bench fit is unsuitable, use supported standing bent-knee calf raises instead, same reps/rest, and log changed knee angle.
P.job: Maintain controlled knee-flexed ankle strength separately from E1's fast light task.

P.name: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise — supported single leg
P.cue: Work from floor, near-straight soft knee, one DB and stable hand support. Rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Reduce load or use bodyweight for lost range; use 1 × 8 bilateral instead of per-leg work if even unilateral bodyweight is too demanding, with 1 × 4 bilateral preparation.
P.job: Maintain the established straight-knee calf strength exposure without flight.

P.name: Dumbbell Glute Bridge — floor
P.cue: Hands secure a DB across pelvis. From knees bent and feet planted, rise 1 s, hold aligned ribs/pelvis 1 s, lower 2 s. Finish through hip extension, not back arching. Reduce load for lumbar extension or unstable implement.
P.job: Use a supported hip-extension finish to retain challenging force work without a long walkout demand.
P.decision: One 1 × 8 loaded floor bridge replaces the four-cycle walkout role for this no-impact support class. Select actual resistance for technical reserve; knee-flexor cycle counts are not converted to bridge reps.

P.name: Supine Band-resisted Hip Flexion
P.cue: Secure loop band around both forefeet; nonworking leg straight with heel grounded. Flex working hip/knee toward thigh-vertical in 2 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s without arching or moving the anchor heel. Reduce tension/range for pelvic tilt. If a secure loop is unavailable, use seated DB hip flexion instead with hands securing the DB above the knee: same dose/rest, small controlled thigh lift; preparation unloaded.
P.job: Retain challenging supported hip-flexor force for leg recovery.

equipment: Band anchors/attachments in E4/E5 must be verified secure; the supplied inventory does not confirm them. Use unresisted supported hip-extension drives instead of E4 if the anchor is unavailable, same count/tempo/rest. Use heel-supported fast forefoot lifts against gravity instead of E5, same count/tempo/rest, if no safe anchored band fits. E6 may be unresisted instead if no suitable loop exists. All remain brief rapid-force practice but changed resistance is logged, not claimed equivalent. Choose stable hand-support heights and a comfortable floor surface for E2; no treadmill, sled, cable station or running lane traversal is needed.
count_note: Zero planned jump landings, zero sprint/running metres. Rapid force efforts are twelve bent-knee heel rises, four long-lever hip drives, six retained-ball drives, eight hip-extension drives, eight dorsiflexion lifts and eight abduction lifts = 46 nonflight efforts. They are not zero-dose explosive slots: each has fast concentric intent and a controlled return. The primary block has six challenging rounds with both sides accounted; lighter S holds total 30 arch seconds plus ten adduction reps.
novelty: Default rapid tasks introduce standing single-leg knee-flexed ankle force, a longer-knee hip-drive lever, retained split-base implement acceleration, isolated resisted hip extension, resisted dorsiflexion and grounded lateral hip acceleration. The held-ball task was previously a contingency and may not be novel if actually used; that history is unknown. Several are declared force/support variants rather than new families. Familiar light control work intentionally recurs under the user's allowance for strength continuity.
audit: Kept all six rapid slots meaningful while removing planned flight; did not relabel a steady hold or slow strengthening rep as explosive. Rejected added jump novelty before the final comparison. Each band-dependent task has a lower-resistance same-action option, and that lower load is not equated with the default. Primary work remains challenging despite the small one-round allocation; the class is not assumed to be a medically indicated deload or a competition taper.
progression: No exercise/load progression is earned without actual response. Use this support-focused prescription when current readiness and schedule suit it; it does not guarantee recovery. Class 12 should return the original ankle marker and selected strength anchors under matching conditions, with deliberate repeat exceptions documented rather than inventing a new test.
map_note: No planned flight; brief rapid-force support and six primary working rounds.
next_job: Final matched-condition gym-anchor review, plus full written-sequence audit and honest direct-practice gaps.
handoff: Review Class 11, all saved anchor/workload records and any actual feedback; finalize Class 12, then audit all twelve classes before declaring the written curriculum complete.

final_review: Checked all six rapid-force slots for actual fast concentric work despite zero planned flight. Forty-six nonflight efforts are distinct from the six challenging strength rounds. Band-anchor availability is explicitly unresolved with same-action lower-resistance replacements. This is a planned support option, not an assumed taper, symptom response or proof of recovery.
